To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a reward based E channel migration policy is more effective than a punishment or a forced migration policy, and (2) highly loyal customers exhibit less reactance than less attitudinally loyal customers.

(a) a punishment based E migration strategy causes similar customer reactance as forced migration does, (b) the use of incentives is effective in reducing the level of customer reactance, (c) the use of rewards is more effective than the use of punishments, (d) the level of reactance is lower for highly loyal customers than for less loyal customers and that (e) highly loyal customers are more forgiving toward the bank than less loyal customers.

(i) the E channel migration strategy of rewarding the use of a firm preferred channel is the most effective strategy to stimulate customer use of this channel, (ii) the E channel strategy of punishing customers for not switching to a preferred E channel causes reactance levels similar to those observed in a forced migration strategy, and (iii) highly attitudinally loyal customers exhibit lower levels of reactance than less attitudinally loyal ones.
